work_units.responsibility: Implement scoped Vault site credential lifecycle

findings.claim: Implemented hub-installed luxnix-vault-site-lifecycle contain|rotate|resume FQDN. Containment checks the exact PKI role domain, persists a root-only role-keyed marker, denies the site policy, destroys its Secret ID accessors, and revokes only issued tokens matching both site policy and AppRole metadata. Enrollment and reconciliation share its lock and cannot clear containment; uppercase enrollment names are refused to prevent case aliases.

rotate FQDN --output-directory NEW_DIR requires completed containment, preserves non-secret KV fields, replaces shared_secret using the observed KV v2 CAS version, verifies the resulting value/version, and exports six protected installer-compatible enrollment files. Partial failure requires fresh containment before retry. resume FQDN --accept-consumer-verification requires rotated state and removes only the local marker; explicit luxnix-vault-reconcile-hub-sites FQDN then restores policy.

Certificate issuance now authenticates afresh from AppRole files after the certificate cache check and before issuance, unsetting the expired bootstrap token. Auth errors expose no response details; offline authentication failure may retain only a still-valid matching cached certificate. AppRole token TTLs remain 1h/4h; newly reconciled roles explicitly issue accessor-revocable service tokens.

Verified API semantics for AppRole accessor destruction, token accessor revocation including descendants, and KV v2 compare-and-set. Lifecycle helper sends payloads over stdin and redacts API failures.

Migration requires deploying these wrappers on the authoritative hub, preserving /var/lib/luxnix-vault-site-lifecycle across rebuild/recovery, deploying the fresh-auth client module, and using a reviewed short-lived custodian policy. The policy needs site-bound PKI role/CA reads, site ACL write, role Secret ID list/create/destroy and role-id read, KV node read/write, plus privileged token accessor list/lookup/revoke. Do not put the affected site policy on the operator token. Deliver the new bundle over authenticated encrypted transport, update both NetworkNode consumers and verify old rejection, then resume/reconcile and restart the dependent client chain.

Integration review identified that ordinary timer restart retains a still-valid revoked cached certificate. Added root-only luxnix-vault-reissue-hub-client-certificate on hub-PKI clients: runtime force marker bypasses cache checks and all offline success fallbacks, is cleared only after publishing certificate/key/CA, and is retained after authentication/issuance failure. No certificate is revoked automatically.

gaps: No live Vault, host, credential, deployment, consumer database or remote-state operation was performed. Actual new-machine enrollment, old-ID/token rejection, both node-record adoption, offline recovery and elapsed breach recovery time require controlled operator acceptance.
Full host derivation evaluation/build and repository configuration checks remain root integration work; only module syntax and host discovery were run by this worker.

Containment markers coordinate these hub-local wrappers; other administrative Vault sessions and alternate hubs must be serialized and must not overwrite the deny policy. Preserve the marker directory in disaster recovery. Vault audit destination and custodian ownership remain operator requirements.

Accessor enumeration cannot enumerate pre-existing batch tokens. Review deployed AppRole token types and await their bounded expiry or use explicit custodian containment before restoring policy. Service tokens with unexpected policy provenance cause a fail-closed blocker; accessor lookup races with expiry may require rerunning containment.

Certificate revocation and receiver enforcement are a separate worker boundary. Keep network/application containment until certificate and application rejection are demonstrated. No retiring KV versions are destroyed; retained history requires custodian retention policy.

Role names retain the existing punctuation-normalizing mapping for compatibility. Exact-domain checks and role-keyed containment prevent accidental scoped revocation/containment bypass, but operators must not enroll colliding FQDN aliases as distinct sites.

Forced-reissue marker is under /run and survives service failure, not reboot. Rerun the explicit helper after a reboot until replacement acceptance completes; preserve network/application containment. Node provisioning is RemainAfterExit=true and needs an explicit restart on both consumers.

findings.claim: Receiver transfer locations require ssl_crl and a runtime freshness gate. Bootstrap requires authenticated CRL publication before Nginx startup; a separate 60-second refresh timer reloads Nginx and closes transfers on refresh/reload failure. TLS resumption is disabled for the receiver virtual host and transfer locations limit keepalive to one request.

Publisher requires pinned HTTPS publisher authentication, refuses redirects and credential-bearing URLs, validates complete direct CRLs signed by every pinned client CA, enforces time bounds and CRL-number rollback protection, and publishes atomically without replacing the prior bundle on validation failure.

uv run pytest -q tests/test_hub_client_revocation.py: exit 0, 10 passed in 1.28s. Real disposable Nginx accepted the old certificate before revocation, rejected it after CRL publication and reload, accepted its replacement, rejected unknown publisher TLS CA, and returned 503 after gate removal. Other cases cover incomplete chains, wrong signatures, future/stale/expired CRLs, rollback and insecure endpoints.

Official Nginx documentation requires intermediate CRLs in the same PEM file as the leaf issuer CRL; Vault exposes public CRL endpoints, whose transport is authenticated here without a bearer token.

gaps: No live hosts contacted or production certificates revoked. Controlled receiver rejection and measured propagation/recovery time remain operator acceptance requirements.

Root integration must run full Nix evaluation with the untracked helper included in its source snapshot and integrate operator documentation. Individual Nix parse checks do not establish systemd boot/reload behavior.

Initial rollout requires existing independently pinned Vault TLS CA, client CA bundle and an available direct HTTPS CRL endpoint before Nginx can start. Custom/intermediate CA deployments must supply one CRL URL per issuer; missing issuer CRLs fail closed.

CRL age defaults to 72 hours to match Vault defaults. Custodians should configure a shorter Vault CRL expiry and automatic rebuild then lower crlMaxAgeSeconds; the timer polls every 60 seconds, and any attempted refresh failure closes new transfer requests immediately. If the timer is stopped or disabled, OpenSSL CRL nextUpdate expiry remains the hard bound.

Graceful Nginx reload does not terminate already-running uploads or other existing requests. Immediate breach containment still needs trusted receiver/network actions, followed by rejection tests. Shared browser sessions lose TLS resumption; only transfer locations lose HTTP keepalive.

Nginx is reloaded after publication; successful systemctl reload does not itself prove application acceptance. Runtime tests cover real Nginx CRL behavior, not a complete NixOS VM boot or failure-injected systemd reload.

First disposable Nginx attempt failed because ambient LD_LIBRARY_PATH mixed incompatible Nix glibc versions. The isolated test subprocess now removes LD_LIBRARY_PATH and LD_PRELOAD; rerun passes with real Nginx 1.28.0.

work_units.responsibility: Make local vault encryption use explicit key identities

findings.claim: Local encryption and authenticated updates use exactly Vault.key and luxnix-master through Ansible VaultLib; no ambient identity discovery or plaintext temporary files. Host exports use the unique registered PSK identity; unknown, duplicate, or master-labeled host identities fail closed.

Vault.load_dir honors explicit key/directory arguments instead of persisted paths. Vault.validate_local_key checks the private nonempty master key and decrypts all metadata-listed secrets before caller writes.
Admin validation uses the explicit master identity and strict password input loading. Legacy ciphertext fails with an explicit migration requirement.

Explicit per-file migration authenticates legacy ciphertext using one specified key/label, verifies newly encrypted master ciphertext, refuses existing output, and retains all source ciphertext, keys, and metadata. It does not publish a vault or exports.

Migration is per-file and intentionally non-destructive. Operator must inventory all legacy ciphertext and exact key mappings, retain encrypted backups and old keys, stage every verified copy in a new vault, review/update copied vault.yml absolute secret paths, validate the complete new vault, then switch as one reviewed operation before exporting. No automatic mixed-key fallback or metadata path rewrite is provided.

Existing keys that grant group/other permissions now fail; the custodian must review and correct private key handling before operations. Missing existing keys must be recovered rather than regenerated.

work_units.responsibility: Remove shared password fallback from secure host defaults

findings.claim: Removed embedded shared admin hashes and all write-on-missing fallback behavior; legacy fallback configuration is rejected at evaluation.

Admin activation checks require an existing regular root-owned mode0400/0600 single-line SHA512 crypt or yescrypt hash, and reject the retired shared credential by fingerprint. Missing/invalid files abort before users activation without creating replacements.

The real gc-05 configuration evaluates with fallback disabled, password SSH disabled, four admin authorized keys, no failed assertions, and users activation ordered after validation. Explicit alternate recovery-file selection and SOPS pre-user dependency ordering evaluate successfully.

Fleet-impacting default: all admin-module consumers now require their runtime hash before activation, including hosts outside gc-* and configurations disabling security.luxnix.local-users.

Before new-host installation or upgrade, provision a unique per-host SHA512 crypt or yescrypt hash in the configured runtime path, root-owned mode0400/0600 inside a protected directory, through documented secret delivery. Never place it in inventory, Nix source, or the Nix store.

Remove legacy fallback.enable and fallback.hashedPassword settings in either namespace. Disabling adminPassword.requireUsableFile and overriding credential fields via user.admin.extraOptions now fail evaluation.
Rotate any installed retired shared fallback before activation; the old hash is refused even when already present in the runtime file.
Verify independent authorized SSH key login and privilege escalation or console/installer recovery before rollout; keep a unique offline recovery credential in operator custody independent of Vault.

For explicitly selected offline recovery, provision the separate unique file out of band and select security.luxnix.local-users.adminPassword.hashedFile (or user.admin.passwordFile when policy is disabled). This is an operator-selected credential, not an automatic fallback or restoration of a compromised old credential.
Alternative userborn/sysusers backends are rejected because current validation relies on users activation ordering. Supporting them requires a separate tested pre-user validation integration.
